children: Shares of Sky Quarry climbed after the company said it restarted operations at its Eagle Springs Refinery, located in Nevada.
The stock rose 15%, to $2.91, on Thursday. Despite the gain, shares have lost roughly 15% of their value year to date.

The energy-infrastructure company said before the bell that one of its subsidiaries, Foreland Refining Corp., received an air permit from the Nevada Division of Environmental Protection and has restarted operations at the refinery.

In preparation for the restart, Sky Quarry completed approximately $300,000 in repairs and upgrades to Eagle Springs, which has a stated nameplate capacity of approximately 5,000 barrels of crude oil per day.
Interim Chief Executive Marcus Laun called the restart a major development, as Eagle Springs is Nevada's only crude-oil refinery.

"Nevada has relied on fuel refined elsewhere for too long," he said. "Our job now is to ramp Eagle Springs toward its full operating potential and make Nevada-refined products a more meaningful part of the region's supply."
